answer_text: Hypermetropia is the defect in which a person can see distant objects clearly but cannot focus nearby objects. The image of a near object is formed behind the retina. This happens if the eyeball is too short or if the eye lens is too weak, so its focal length is too long. A convex lens of suitable power adds converging power. The lens forms a virtual image of the nearby object at the person's near point, and the eye then focuses that image on the retina.
